modules.module_description: Learn how water moves around our planet in a continuous cycle!

segments.segment_description: Understanding the different stages of the water cycle.

concept_bullets: The Sun heats up water in oceans, rivers, and lakes.
It turns into invisible water vapor (like steam) that rises into the air.
Plants also release water vapor through tiny holes in their leaves called stomata.

learning_objectives.objective_text: Understand how water turns into vapor

image_examples.image_description: Think about a puddle after it rains. On a sunny day, the puddle gets smaller until it disappears. The water turned into vapor and went up into the sky! Trees also "breathe out" water vapor through their leaves.
image_examples.image_prompt: Educational illustration. A puddle on a sidewalk shrinking under a bright sun, showing wavy lines representing water vapor rising.

other_details.caption: Puddles dry up because the water evaporates.

concept_bullets: Water vapor rises high into the sky where it's very cold.
It cools down and turns back into tiny water droplets.
These millions of tiny droplets cluster together to form clouds.

image_examples.image_description: Breathe on a cold window. You see water droplets form on the glass. That's condensation! Your warm breath (water vapor) hits the cold surface and turns back into liquid water.
image_examples.image_prompt: Educational illustration. A child breathing on a cold window pane, seeing a foggy patch of tiny water droplets form.

other_details.caption: Warm breath condensing on a cold surface.

concept_bullets: Clouds get too heavy with water droplets.
Gravity pulls the water back down to Earth.
It falls as rain, snow, sleet, or hail depending on temperature.

image_examples.image_description: Clouds are like giant sponges floating in the sky. When the sponge gets too full, the water falls down. Warm weather = rain. Cold weather = snow!
image_examples.image_prompt: Educational illustration. A split scene showing rain falling from a cloud on a warm day and snow falling from a cloud on a cold day.

other_details.caption: Precipitation releases water back to Earth.

concept_bullets: Rainwater flows downhill into rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans.
Some water soaks into the ground through soil and rocks.

image_examples.image_description: After rain, water flows down streets into drains. It travels to rivers, then lakes or ocean. Some rainwater soaks into soil where plants drink it.
image_examples.image_prompt: Educational illustration. Rainwater flowing into a drain and soaking into the soil near plants.

other_details.caption: Water collects in bodies of water or soaks into the ground.

segments.segment_description: Discover how heat transfer and water cycle concepts are applied in real life

concept_bullets: The water cycle and heat transfer principles help us conserve water and energy.
Inventions like Ice Stupa and Rainwater Harvesting use these natural cycles.

image_examples.image_description: An innovative water conservation technique where mountain stream water is channeled through underground pipes and sprayed into cold air during winters. The water freezes layer by layer, creating tall cone-shaped ice structures that melt slowly in spring, providing water for farming throughout summer.
image_examples.image_prompt: Photo-realistic illustration of an Ice Stupa in Ladakh.

other_details.caption: Ice Stupa stores water as ice for summer use.
other_details.impact: Provides water supply during water-scarce spring season
other_details.connection: Stores water in solid form (ice) which melts and evaporates.

image_examples.image_description: Systems that collect and store rainwater from rooftops and other surfaces. The collected water is filtered and directed into underground storage tanks or used to recharge groundwater through recharge pits.
image_examples.image_prompt: Diagram of a rainwater harvesting system on a house.

other_details.caption: Collecting rainwater for future use.
other_details.impact: Reduces dependency on municipal water supply
